grants.title: Standard Grants
grants.funder: The Healthcare Foundation of New Jersey (HFNJ)
grants.summary: Strongest match found. HFNJ funds at-risk/underserved health programs in greater Newark and the Jewish Federation of Greater MetroWest NJ footprint, which per search results covers Essex, Morris, Somerset, Union and parts of Sussex counties — overlapping three of the four priority counties. Recent priorities reportedly emphasize youth mental health and behavioral health. Next quarterly deadline is 9 days out; Nov 21 is the following cycle.
grants.verify_before_acting: Confirm the Aug 28 deadline, whether a non-Jewish-affiliated org in Union/Somerset qualifies under the 'targeted vulnerable populations elsewhere' clause, and any audit requirement.

grants.title: Special One-time Grants
grants.funder: The Healthcare Foundation of New Jersey (HFNJ)
grants.summary: Rolling-deadline companion to HFNJ's standard program, same geography. Lower ceiling but no cycle to wait for — a plausible first approach to this funder given the org is open to awards of any size.
grants.verify_before_acting: Confirm rolling status and eligibility geography.

grants.title: Small Grants (rolling)
grants.summary: CFNJ reviews small grant requests up to $15,000 on a rolling basis through its grants management system, funding nonprofits promoting healthier individuals and communities statewide. Note: its dedicated children's behavioral health funding is reportedly earmarked for Sussex and Morris counties, outside the priority footprint — the general health track is the relevant door.
grants.verify_before_acting: Confirm the general health track is open to Essex/Bergen/Union/Somerset applicants.

grants.title: 2026 Arts & Community Health Request for Proposals
grants.funder: The Horizon Foundation for New Jersey
grants.summary: Annual RFP released June 1, 2026; decisions communicated December 2026 with funded programs starting January 1, 2027. Open to organizations whose mission promotes health in New Jersey communities. Partial fit — the 'Arts & Community Health' framing may or may not accommodate a pure behavioral-health education program.
grants.verify_before_acting: Find the actual submission deadline (not surfaced in search) and confirm behavioral health education is in scope. NOTE: requires a current satisfactory CPA financial audit for ALL applicants including those under $500k income — a real cost/feasibility gate for a $300k-budget org.

grants.title: Pathways to Recovery
grants.funder: NJ Department of Labor and Workforce Development
grants.summary: Provides training, career services, and supportive services to NJ residents impacted by opioid use. Eligible applicants reportedly include nonprofits with connections to mental health and opioid use disorder treatment centers — which the org's treatment-provider partnerships would support. Pre-application periods reportedly opened Jan 26, 2026 (spring) and mid-June 2026 (fall).
grants.verify_before_acting: Determine whether the fall cycle is still open as of late August 2026.

recurring_programs_to_watch.program: SAMHSA Treatment, Recovery, and Workforce Support (TI-26-009)
recurring_programs_to_watch.why: Deadline July 23, 2026 has passed. $10.5M program, max $500k per award, 21 awards, open to private nonprofits providing SUD/COD treatment and recovery services in partnership with local/state stakeholders — a close fit. Watch for the FY2027 cycle.

recurring_programs_to_watch.program: BJA Second Chance Act — Community-Based Reentry Program
recurring_programs_to_watch.why: FY25 cycle closed May 2026. $500k-$750k awards, explicitly open to nonprofit community-based organizations serving reentry populations — arguably the single best-fit federal program for this org. Watch for the next solicitation.
State behavioral health authority; Integrated Care Program RFP closed July 17, 2026. This page is the primary source for NJ state behavioral health procurements and should be checked every run.

2026 awards to 41 organizations announced July 6, 2026 — that cycle is closed. Funds housing, employment prep, case management, and behavioral/mental health support for reentry. Structured around municipalities hiring a Reentry Coordinator, so the likely route here is subgrantee/service-provider partnership with a funded municipality rather than direct application.
